name: Criterion matrix
reader_question: Which options meet which stated criteria, and where is the evidence silent?
relationship: Categorical assessment of each option against each criterion; no aggregation across criteria.
use_when: Each cell can be graded Meets, Partly, Does not or Not stated from a cited source
The reader needs to see evidential gaps next to failures
avoid_when: A weighted total or ranking is wanted — the tracker has no synthetic scores; use ranked-bar on a sourced measure
Criteria are quantities on a shared unit — use a native table or bar chart

data_contract.notes: One option to highlight; must be an option label

data_contract.type: Meets | Partly | Does not | Not stated
data_contract.notes: One mark per option, in option order

units: No units: categorical marks only. Weights, scores and totals are rejected.

not_data_bound: The circle glyphs (filled, half, hollow, dashed) are native shapes positioned over the mark cells from fixed row heights; changing a mark in the table does not move or redraw its glyph

table_alternative: The native table itself, with the glyph column removed and marks as text.
variations: Role-matrix when the cells name roles rather than grades
limitations: Four fixed marks; finer grading would imply a scale the sources do not support
Marks assert nothing beyond the cited statement; they do not combine into an overall verdict

excluded_alternatives.reason: A total invents a cross-criterion scale and hides evidential gaps
Requires numeric scores on a common axis
